processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Hot torsion test performed in a direction involving a negative shear, under argon atmosphere to reduce oxidation phenomena. This condition (1000 °C, 0.1 s−1) is one of a series of torsion tests over 900–1100 °C and 0.1–10 s−1; at this condition strain levels of approximately ε = 1 to ε = 25 were examined (Fig. 1 shows ε = 1, 2, 5, 25). Condition under which continuous dynamic recrystallization (CDRX) operates.

After deformation, samples were quenched immediately (0.5 s) with argon in order to retain the microstructures and avoid post-dynamic recrystallization. The cooling rate is ~200 °C s−1 during the first seconds.

structures.overall_structure: Hot-torsion deformed Fe–8% Al ferritic alloy in which continuous dynamic recrystallization (CDRX) operates. The original large grains are progressively elongated along the shear direction and subdivided by subgrain boundaries. Subgrain boundaries progressively transform into grain boundaries with increasing strain, so the initial large-grain microstructure is progressively replaced by a much finer 'recrystallized' one and the volume fraction of grain boundaries strongly increases. Fragmentation is selective (some grains more fragmented than others). At intermediate strain the material is an 'aggregate of crystallites' bounded partly by low angle boundaries (LABs) and partly by high angle boundaries (HABs).

phases_present.phase_name: ferrite (Fe–8% Al, A2 non-ordered bcc solid solution)
phases_present.morphology: Large original grains, clearly visible, elongated in the direction of the shear

grain_structure.texture: Misorientation distribution at low strain (Fig. 2a): LAB (θ < 15°) = 85%, HAB (θ ≥ 15°) = 15%, average misorientation angle = 9.4°
